course_name_original: Técnicas de Expresión Oral y Escrita en Inglés
course_name_en: Oral and Written Expression Techniques in English
prerequisites: Prior knowledge of English grammatical and linguistic structures
Communicative competence level B2 according to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages

learning_outcomes.text: Follow and give simple oral presentations, making correct use of intonation and expressive possibilities.
Request and offer services related to the work environment, using varied, precise, and appropriate vocabulary for the situation.
Participate in meetings and seminars by taking notes, expressing own ideas, and making proposals.
Handle routine requests for goods or services over the phone.
Draft and understand formal reports and common professional correspondence in accordance with established rhetorical, grammatical, and lexical norms.

syllabus_topics: Preparation of technical reports: structure and linguistic characteristics
Participating in socio-professional activities within the company:
Conducting job interviews and presenting CVs
Participating in debates, meetings, and negotiations
Use of language and linguistic signaling techniques
Use of visual aids and body language
Use of voice: rhythm and emphasis

assessment_methods.method: Partial exam (E1): Written individual exam on a cover letter
Practical work (T1): Submission of individual Curriculum Vitae
Partial exam (E2): Oral individual exam on a simulated job interview
Practical work (T2): Written technical report prepared jointly by two or more students
Partial exam (E3): Written exam on the technical report (linguistic and content aspects)
Partial exam (E4): Group debate participation (individually assessed)
Partial exam (E5): Individual oral presentation on technological innovation in engineering
Class participation (C1): Active participation in practical sessions (minimum 80% attendance required)

assessment_rules: For the ordinary examination, the final grade is calculated as the sum of E1 + T1 + E2 + T2 + E3 + E4 + E5 + E6 + C1. To pass the subject, a minimum final grade of 5 is required. There is no minimum grade for individual components. For extraordinary examinations, the final grade is calculated as P1+P2+P3+P4+T1, where P1 (written questions on a cover letter) is 10%, P2 (written questions on a CV) is 10%, P3 (oral exam on a simulated job interview) is 20%, P4 (listening comprehension exam) is 20%, and T1 (written and orally defended technical report) is 40%. A minimum final grade of 5 is required to pass, and no grades are carried over from the ordinary examination.
